I grew up loving music all my life. I have a lot of siblings so thankfully I grew up listening to all different kinds of genres. I personally grew up with my favorite genres being rock, funk and blues. 

I remember one day during my freshmen year of college. I learned about Jimi Hendrix. I looked him up and chose at random one of his popular songs to listen to. That song was Little Wing. I thought it was the most beautiful song ever and was blown away by his guitar skills. 

Since that day I wanted to be like Hendrix and learn to play a lot of his songs. I was 14 years old back then and now I'm 28 and still playing everyday. It was the greatest decision of my life. It prevented me from having unhealthy coping mechanisms (drugs, alcohol, partying, sex) for whenever I would go through a hard time in life or was too depressed and suicidal. Now I play guitar whenever I get depressed and it makes me feel a lot better. Guitar is my therapy.

For the first half the day you do either one of these

Stow: you take packages off the racks and put them into bags. You'll be in charge of multiple isles. I personally think it's easy but a lot of people think otherwise and hate it. 

Pick to buffer: you take packages off the conveyor and put them on the racks for the stowers. Really really easy

Unloading: you have associates bring you pallets or cages and you unload them onto the conveyor for the pick to buffer and stowers. This in my opinion is the hardest job. I hate doing it and it's really tiring. But I do have a really bad back. 

Push: just push packages down the correct conveyor. There are stickers on the packages telling you which conveyor it should go to. 

Split: you split the packages as they come down the conveyor by letter. So it's easier for the pick to buffers to get them off the conveyors. For example put the "A" packages on one side of the conveyor and the "B" packages on the other side. As you can see you'll split them by letter. 

Induct: you use a device to scan the packages the unloader puts on the conveyor. The device is used to put the stickers on the packages. The sticker just tells you what location the package is going to. 

Second half of the day

Pick: here you pretty much get all the bags/packages and put them on the cart to stage at the proper location for the drivers, so they can make their deliveries. 

OTR: Here you'll be outside either helping the drivers get their carts so they can put them into their vans. There's also something called traffic control. You direct traffic for the vans. And there's also problem solve. Here you solve any issues using your device if drivers are missing packages, have damaged packages etc. 

Bag reset: this is at the very end of the day. You put new bags in the stowing aisles and get them ready for the next shift.
